title: The V1 playtest notes: waves that climb into the hundreds, Isao mending the base between waves, and an eased hull steering
context: The owner playtested the published V1 session and sent three notes: the waves are much too easy ("slow start, then it should start getting hectic... hundreds of low levels, a few more hardcores"), Isao never rebuilds the gate or the walls the swarm breaks, and the tank turns too sharply. A fourth note asked whether the plasma thrower should be gate-locked behind a technology discovery. The session the owner played is a bare index.html.
outcome: Three fixes, one finding. (1) DIFFICULTY had two independent causes. readStoryQuery treated a bare index.html as a deep link and handed it the sparse 0.35 threat multiplier meant for inspecting a jumped-to stage, so the owner fought a third of the swarm the sector table asks for: sector 1 opened with two bodies alive and the whole six-sector run peaked at 54 concurrent. Only an explicit ?stage= or ?story= keeps the sparse waves now. Separately the table capped every programme at ladder wave 8, below computeWavePlan's invasion surge - the only thing in the ladder that puts low-belt bodies on the ground in the hundreds - which made late waves SHRINK rather than swell (a sector-3 wave went 90 bodies, then 66, because the headline turns non-rammable and its density rule halves instead of multiplying). The ladder windows now climb through the surge and the hard cores are a small explicit count (SECTORS[n].hardcores) instead of the twenty-odd solid bodies the surge throws in on its own. (2) ISAO REPAIRS: a new pure rule (src/domain/repair-orders.js) queues the gate first, then the blown-out wall cells in rim order, only while no wave is running and never ahead of an order the player placed; it rides his existing travel-and-print loop and he says one line the first time. (3) STEERING: the steer keys wrote the full yaw rate on the frame they went down and zero on the frame they came up - a step function, not a fast tank. src/domain/steer-ease.js ramps the same top rate over an attack constant and releases it over a shorter one, and the hull banks into the turn through the hover rig's existing roll channel. (4) The PLASMA THROWER is ALREADY gated and was left alone: it is the `plasma` tower (src/lore.js:161 names it PLASMA THROWER), unlocked only by bringing the 'coil stack' part home from expedition site rocket-c, itself hidden until three parts are in (src/content/story-defaults.js:100), with the refusal reading PART NOT HOME (src/td-tab.js:6819). The MORK's hold-to-sweep secondary is called 'plasma' in tutorial text but is the twin beam rig, not the thrower.
alternatives: Raise the sector threat numbers alone and leave the 0.35 bare-page multiplier: rejected, it fights the wrong lever - the content table was already asking for three times what the owner was fighting.

Keep ladderCap at 8 and grow difficulty only through threat: rejected, it cannot reach hundreds of low-belt bodies, because the amoeba/ghost re-flood lives only above ladder wave 8, and it leaves the late-wave shrink in place.
Generator ladderCap 12 with threatStep 0.25: measured, rejected at 718 concurrent in sector 6 - past what the frame budget holds. Cap 11 / step 0.2 tops out at 490.
Make the tank turn more slowly: rejected, the owner asked for smoothing, not a slower hull; the top yaw rate is unchanged at 2.6 rad/s.
Repair the gate passively through mendGate alone: rejected, the owner asked for Isao to go and build, so the trip is the fix and the passive trickle stays as it was.
evidence: Node harness over sectorDef + computeWavePlan, per sector and wave (scratchpad difficulty.mjs). BEFORE at the bare page's real 0.35 multiplier: S1 opens 2 alive, peaks 10; run peak 54 concurrent; 1012 bodies S1-S6. BEFORE at threat 1: run peak 144, and sector 3 fell 90 -> 66 in its last two waves.
AFTER (bare page now runs at 1): S1 8/16/28/38, S2 38/54/64/72, S3 74/80/254/308/374/374, generated sectors plateau at 490; 9838 bodies S1-S6; every sector's biggest wave beats the last one's.
Harness cross-validated against the real spawner: it predicted 1464 bodies for sector 3's whole programme, the browser reported 1496 alive.
Browser, source build, scripts/browser-test.mjs --waves --last through browser-lock.sh: sector 3's biggest single wave measured 406 concurrent at p50 20.9 ms, p95 46 ms, max 72.7 ms over 474 frames.
Browser, deliberate overload (--waves, whole programme released at once): 1496 concurrent at p50 24.4 ms, p95 53 ms, max 146 ms over 392 frames.

npm test: 118 test programs passed, including new test/steer-ease.mjs and test/repair-orders.mjs and the reshaped test/sectors.mjs (which now pins the climb: sector 1 opens gently, every sector peaks harder than the last, sector 3 fights in the hundreds, nothing past 520).
npm run check: architecture guard, line budgets and top-level placement hold; src/td-tab.js unchanged at its 13506 budget (10 insertions, 10 deletions).
